Derazhnya Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Derazhnya's Jewish community, documented from 1550, included a Karaite community that perished during the Khmelnytsky massacre, with survivors fleeing to Bar, documented elsewhere in this collection. In 1757, Talmud books belonging to Derazhnya's Jews and other communities in the region were burned in the square at Kamyanets-Podilskyi, a consequence of the dispute between Orthodox rabbis and Jacob Frank, documented elsewhere in this collection. In the 1810s-30s, local Jews supported the rebel units of the famous Ukrainian outlaw leader Ustym Karmaliuk. The ghetto's liquidation in September-October 1941 saw over 1,500 Jews shot; a memorial was opened at the site in September 1970. This is the older of Derazhnya's two Jewish cemeteries.
